children: A divided U.S. government can support Treasurys by limiting further fiscal expansion, Vontobel's Andrew Jackson says in a note as Republicans lost their majority in both chambers. "But blocking new spending is not the same as reducing the existing deficit," the head of investments says. Persistent deficits and heavy Treasury issuance could therefore limit how far long-term yields fall, even with a stronger congressional check on the administration, he says. Inflation and Federal Reserve policy are likely to matter more for bonds than the election results, while any renewed rise in energy prices could complicate the outlook, Jackson says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
